title: Monsoon AI - private egress & region lockdown discovery
summary: Discovery focused on Monsoon AI's need for a private-only deployment with strict region lockdowns, fixed egress IPs, and integration with customer KMS and internal audit tooling. SE went through high-level topology options (VPC peering, transit gateway, private endpoints), Redwood fallbacks, and benchmark/playbook asks. Next steps: security pack + network diagram + pricing ask; pilot proposal for limited traffic in us-west-2 only.
next_steps: Redwood to send security pack (SOC2, ISO, KMS integration notes) by 2026-06-18
Lena to draft topology options and recommended config (peering vs privatelink) by 2026-06-20
Samir to share preliminary pricing for a 3-month dedicated pilot by 2026-06-19
Customer to provide list of allowed egress IPs and region constraint doc by 2026-06-22
Schedule technical benchmark with 1 GPU node and sample prompts week of 2026-06-29
action_items: Lena Ortiz: produce 2 topology diagrams (peering+transit, privatelink) - due 2026-06-20
Samir Patel: email security pack and pilot pricing - due 2026-06-18
Ravi Menon: share legal/regional constraint spreadsheet and egress IP whitelist - due 2026-06-22
transcript:
[00:00] Samir Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. This is Samir from Redwood, AE. We have Lena, our solutions engineer, here. How are you all?
[00:06] Ravi Menon: Doing well, thanks. Morning from SF.
[00:09] Diane Kuo: Afternoon. Excited to talk through the network constraints.
[00:12] Samir Patel: Great. Quick agenda — high level constraints, talk through VPC peering/private endpoints options, egress/ips, and then security/compliance asks. Does that work?
[00:20] Marcus Hall: Yep, that works. Our ask up front — Monsoon's legal/regulatory requires us to keep inference traffic inside us-west-2 and we need fixed egress IPs for allowlisting. Also, keys must be customer-managed.
[00:32] Lena Ortiz: Okay noted. On the region side, Redwood supports region pinning for Private so you can restrict to us-west-2. For egress IPs, there are a couple options — NAT/GW on your side with peering, or use our private endpoint + static egress block through our transit — depends on whether you want control in your VPC.
[00:48] Diane Kuo: We're leaning toward us controlling egress. Our security team doesn't want provider-routed egress unless it's in a limited pool we can audit.
[00:56] Samir Patel: Makes sense. One common pattern we see is: deploy Redwood Private (control plane outside but customer-managed dataplane in VPC), peering to our inference subnets via VPC peering or TGW, then you NAT through your owned egress. That gives you IPs to whitelist.
[01:12] Marcus Hall: What's the difference if we use PrivateLink / interface endpoints instead? I thought that gives private connectivity without peering.
[01:18] Lena Ortiz: Right — PrivateLink (AWS PrivateLink) creates ENIs in your VPC and you hit the provider via those endpoints. Pros: no peering, less route table footprint. Cons: if you need high throughput or multi-AZ scaling, you might need multiple endpoints and there's per-GB cost. Also, some customers prefer peering + TGW for centralized routing, especially if they already use a transit architecture.
[01:40] Ravi Menon: We're concerned about throughput and latency — low 100ms tail latency is a goal for some of our user flows. How does Private compare to Dedicated for latency?
[01:48] Lena Ortiz: Dedicated capacity gives you pinned GPUs in a Redwood-managed pool — lower jitter and more predictable tails because hardware is reserved. Private in VPC can be almost as low latency if collocated and we avoid cross-AZ hairpins, but it's more configuration dependent. If you need SLAs on 99th percentile latency, Dedicated is the safer bet.
[02:06] Diane Kuo: For cost reasons we'd prefer Private if it doesn't blow the SLOs. Can you show a topology that keeps egress under our control and limits cross-region traffic?
[02:14] Lena Ortiz: Absolutely. I'll lay out two options: 1) VPC peering + your NAT/GW (you control egress IPs), 2) PrivateLink with policy-based routing to your NAT (smaller trust boundary but more endpoints). I'll annotate throughput tradeoffs and gateway limits.
[02:29] Marcus Hall: Also send us details on how KMS is integrated. We want customer-managed CMKs; we need assurance that keys aren't exported and audit logs are complete.
[02:38] Samir Patel: Redwood supports customer KMS for Private deployments; logs can be forwarded to your SIEM and we have audit trails in our control plane too. We'll include our KMS integration doc in the security pack.
[02:48] Diane Kuo: Do you support bringing your own HSM? We have an HSM-backed key policy with our KMS provider.
[02:53] Lena Ortiz: For Private we can integrate with external KMS/HSMs — usually via IAM and KMS grants. We'll need to validate the key rotation policy during the pilot.
[03:03] Ravi Menon: On egress, if we use your private endpoint and you have a failover region, does traffic ever cross into another region?
[03:09] Lena Ortiz: By default we try to keep traffic in-region if you pin to a region. For hosted fallbacks we might cross to a nearby region if there's an outage, but for Private we'll honor the region restriction if you configure strict routing and pin the model version to the regional cluster. We can also disable cross-region failover for stricter compliance.
[03:28] Marcus Hall: Good. We need to see the controls in writing — where is that toggle?
[03:31] Samir Patel: We'll include the operability section in the pack and call it out in the topology doc.
[03:35] Speaker 4: (inaudible)
[03:36] Lena Ortiz: Another item — egress bandwidth planning. If you intend to do batch embedding generation, you may need higher NAT throughput; we recommend sizing the NAT/GW and considering parallel ENIs or a dedicated egress appliance. We'll provide a guidance table.
[03:51] Diane Kuo: For benchmarks, we plan to run 50 tps small-chat traffic and a nightly batch of 20k embeddings. Want to ensure that Private won't throttle us.
[03:59] Lena Ortiz: For 50 tps chat, both Private and Dedicated can handle it; batching embeddings is more throughput-bound. For embeddings, we usually recommend Dedicated for sustained high throughput or use autoscaling in Private with burst capacity. We'll outline autoscaling knobs and how they interact with your VPC limits.
[04:17] Ravi Menon: One sticky point — legal wants proofs that data doesn't leave the allowed region and that logs are accessible to us. Can Redwood produce an architecture diagram with layers labeled and a list of audit logs we can consume?
[04:28] Samir Patel: Yes — we'll include diagrams and a log manifest: control plane audit logs, dataplane flow logs, KMS access logs, and API audit trails. We can also provide examples of S3 lifecycle, if relevant.
[04:39] Marcus Hall: Also, how does SSO/SCIM integrate? We use Okta and we need RBAC mapped to our groups.
[04:45] Lena Ortiz: Redwood has SAML/SCIM for SSO and RBAC. For Private we can integrate with your IdP; provisioning can be automated. We'll include a sample SAML metadata file and SCIM mapping examples.
[04:55] Diane Kuo: What about routing from our on-prem data center — we have a transit VPC with a VGW peering into AWS. Do you support transitive routing across TGW?
[05:03] Lena Ortiz: AWS doesn't allow transitive peering. If you use TGW and attach both your VPC and the Red-wood-private VPC, TGW can handle the routing. Alternatively, we can put endpoints in each spoke. We'll diagram both.
[05:16] Ravi Menon: Any known gotchas?
[05:18] Lena Ortiz: A few: large model KV cache warming across AZ boundaries can cause extra egress if KV cache isn't local; ensure cache residency in same AZ for low latency. Also, PrivateLink costs can add up for high throughput. Finally, plan for route table limits and ENI quotas.
[05:33] Marcus Hall: That aligns with our ops notes.
[05:35] Samir Patel: On procurement, what's your timeline?
[05:38] Ravi Menon: We want a pilot as proof-of-concept in Q3, legal review in parallel. If pilot looks good we expect to commit to Dedicated or a multi-AZ Private deployment.
[05:47] Samir Patel: Great — we'll aim the pilot for a single-region, single-AZ Private deployment with your NAT egress. Pilot sizing — we recommend 1 x t4-gpu equivalent for inference tests and an autoscaled embedding worker for nightly runs.
[05:59] Diane Kuo: For the pilot, can we whitelist a small set of egress IPs to test integration with our downstream services?
[06:04] Lena Ortiz: Yes — provide the CIDR / IPs you need and we'll validate flows. We'll also run a quick connectivity checklist during onboarding.
[06:12] Speaker 2 (Ravi): One question on pricing — if we lock to Private for region compliance but want burst capacity to Dedicated during peak, is hybrid routing possible?
[06:21] Samir Patel: We support smart routing policies — you can prefer Private but fall back to Dedicated or hosted for overflow. For compliance you can disable overflow. We'll show policy examples in the playbook.
[06:33] Marcus Hall: Competitors we evaluated offered similar features but lacked the combined audits with KMS customer keys. That's a reason we're exploring Redwood.
[06:41] Samir Patel: Appreciate that. We'll highlight those differences.
[06:44] Lena Ortiz: I'll follow up with two diagrams and a network checklist. Samir will send the security pack and pricing.
[06:50] Diane Kuo: Please include the egressization checklist — NAT size, ENI counts, routes to TGW.
[06:56] Samir Patel: Will do. Any other items?
[06:59] Speaker 3 (Marcus): Can you include a sample SLA for latency and uptime during the pilot?
[07:04] Samir Patel: Yes, we'll include a pilot SLA table and SLO targets.
[07:08] Ravi Menon: Thanks, everyone. We'll review docs and aim to turn around the legal pack in two weeks.
[07:14] Samir Patel: Thanks — talk soon.
[46:00] End of recording
notes: Customer emphasized strict region-only requirement and customer-controlled egress. SE to provide two topologies and cost/throughput tradeoffs. Security team wants KMS/HSM details and audit log manifest. Pilot planned for Q3 with fixed egress IP whitelist testing.
